differences.text: The `collapsible` and `resizable` object props become flat attributes (`collapsed`, `no-collapse-button`, `collapse-button-label`, `default-width`, `min-width`, `max-width`, `auto-save-id`). The user's collapse or resize asks with a cancelable `tct-collapse-change` (or reports `tct-size-change`); writing `collapsed`, `collapse()` or `expand()` never emits. There is one `collapsed` state, so upstream's conflict of two props carrying collapse state cannot occur.

Every collapsed rail item is named by its label and shows a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus; an item with sub-items is a button that opens a named flyout (`role="dialog"`, the localised sub-menu label), on hover (fine pointers), Enter, Space or a click, with focus moving in and Escape returning it. Items without an icon are hidden in the rail, and collapsed sub-items are `inert`.

The render mode is a context (`sideNavRenderContext`) read through `SideNavRenderModeController`. The side navigation derives `drawer` from the enclosing `tct-app-shell` itself; its parts read what it publishes, so an item inside a `footer-icons` or drawer subtree never re-derives it. `topbar` is available only through an explicit provider.
No truncation tooltip on long labels (upstream shows none in the expanded navigation either): the label ellipsizes and the full text stays in the accessibility tree.

The mobile drawer is filled by the shell. Below 768 px the side navigation is slotted into the shell's automatic drawer, renders as full rows without the collapse button or the resize handle, and closes the drawer when a link or a button item is chosen; a `tct-mobile-nav` of your own in the shell's `mobile-nav` slot keeps the inline navigation.

requests.reason: A context consumer that connects before its provider has upgraded, or that is slotted into a shadow tree the provider renders (a footer icon in `footer-icons`, an action in `actions`), can miss the value: the request event is dispatched once. Retry the request when a provider connects on the flat tree (or when the host is assigned to a slot). Until then the side navigation and the item call `renderOnConnect` (side-nav/nav-render.ts) to provide the compact size before the slotted children connect.

differences.text: The menu is a disclosure panel: the trigger has `aria-expanded` and is named "Open menu" (localised), the panel is the slotted content with its own semantics, and focus returns to the trigger when it closes. In the collapsed rail the heading is its icon alone, named by `heading`, with a tooltip.

The interaction boundary follows what is set, as upstream: only `heading-href` is one link; several hrefs are independent links; a menu and no hrefs make the whole heading the trigger; a menu with hrefs keeps the links and adds the chevron button. Closing the menu when a slotted `tct-nav-heading-menu` item is chosen needs a close context from that element (in-page navigation family); plain links close it through the click.

requests.reason: Once `tct-nav-heading-menu` is merged it should read a close request from the heading that hosts it (a context or a `tct-request-close` event) so that choosing an item closes the panel, as choosing a plain link does through the click.

differences.text: The upstream `collapsible` prop is `no-collapse` (inverted) plus the `collapsed` and `has-action` attributes. The user's toggle asks with a cancelable `tct-collapse-change` (`collapsed`, `reason`); writing `collapsed` never emits. The chevron toggle stops the click, so listeners on the item never hear it.

In the collapsed rail an item is a named icon button (label, or a host `aria-label`) with a tooltip; an item with sub-items opens a named flyout dialog. Disabled items are native disabled buttons, or anchors without a destination, out of the tab order.

The row uses the shared navigation-row styling (`nav-row`) with Tecton overlay roles for hover and pressed, the neutral role for selected, and Highlight, HighlightText and GrayText in forced-colours mode.
